results.title: 2026 World Cup Group A Preview: Mexico, South Africa, South Korea & Czechia | RotoWire
highlights:
The March window against Panama gave
[...]
coach Broos
[...]
to solve. They drew 1-1, creating chances but wasting several with Lyle Foster and Bongokuhle Hlongwane both guilty of misses that would have been unforgivable at a higher level. In Cape Town, they lost 2-1 in the second game against Panama after Mbekezeli Mbokazi scored a stunning long-range goal to pull level, only to concede a headed winner from a cross that the defense dealt with poorly. The pressing
[...]
not always there for them. The clinical instinct that wins big games is not guaranteed when Foster has an off night. And the goalscoring problem, with the consistent absence of a reliable backup to Foster when he is not delivering, is the one question he goes into the tournament still trying
[...]
are priced as favorites across
[...]
books, implying roughly a 50 percent chance to win the group
[...]
Czechia and South Korea are consistently positioned close to each other, closely behind Mexico in the group odds with roughly a 20 percent implied probability to win the group.
[...]
| Group A Winner Odds |
| --- |
| Team | FanDuel | BetMGM | DraftKings |
| Mexico | -120 | -110 | -110 |
| Czechia | +310 | +300 | +330 |
| South Korea | +350 | +300 | +350 |
| South Africa | +1,100 | +1,000 | +1,200 |
[...]
Mexico win this group. The home advantage, Azteca in the opener against South Africa, Akron in Guadalajara against South Korea, and Azteca again for the Czechia finale, gives them an edge that no sportsbook can fully quantify. Jimenez in the best form of his career, Alvarez as the midfield anchor, Quinones or Alvarado as wide threats and a collective that coach Aguirre has spent two years shaping into something with genuine character are all pointing in the same direction.
[...]
Second place is where the group gets genuinely interesting. Czechia and South Korea are both priced around the same odds and both have legitimate cases. Czechia have the more reliable defensive foundation and a set-piece threat that will trouble opponents who have not specifically prepared for it. South Korea have the higher individual ceiling with Son, Lee and Kim at their collective best. They are better players than anything Czechia can match at those positions, but the defensive questions from the March window cannot be dismissed.
[...]
The South Korea-Czechia opener on June 11 is the match that determines who finishes second in the group. If South Korea win it, they control their own destiny and Czechia need maximum points from South Africa and Mexico to stay alive. If Czechia win it, South Korea face a significantly harder path. That match is the fulcrum of the group.

results.title: Panama at the 2026 World Cup: Los Canaleros Squad, Key Players & Group L Guide | Fanorate
highlights:
, captain Anibal Godoy, Carr
[...]
Panama are the clear outsiders in Group L, ranked well below England and Croatia. The expanded 48-team format, where the four best third-placed teams advance, offers a slim but real lifeline. Their realistic target is the match against Ghana on June 17 in Toronto — likely the game that defines whether they can compete for a knockout spot.
[...]
For Panama, simply being competitive and avoiding the winless, pointless return of 2018 would mark progress. A win — their first-ever at a World Cup — would be a historic achievement, and sneaking into the round of 32 would be a national triumph.
[...]
Under Thomas Christiansen, Panama are organised, disciplined and pragmatic. Expect a compact defensive block, deep lines against superior opponents, and a reliance on counter-attacks, set-pieces and the leadership of Godoy and Carrasquilla. Christiansen’s long tenure has instilled a clear identity and team cohesion that punches above the squad’s individual quality. The trade-off is limited creativity in sustained attack against deep blocks; Panama are at their best when defending a structure and breaking at speed.
[...]
Panama’s World Cup story is short but emotional. Their debut at Russia 2018 followed a famous qualifying campaign that ended in national celebration. The tournament itself was a brutal lesson at the elite level: a 3–0 loss to Belgium, a
[...]
–1 defeat to England — brightened only by Felipe Baloy’s late goal, the nation’s first-ever at a World Cup — and a 2–1 loss to Tunisia. Panama finished bottom of their group and last in the tournament, conceding eleven goals across three games. The 2026 edition is their chance to write a far more competitive chapter, and to claim a maiden World Cup point or even a first win.
[...]
Panama open their 2026 campaign against Ghana in Toronto and close against England in New Jersey — a 2018 rematch.
[...]
- Underdog romance — a small nation chasing its first-ever World
[...]
can frustrate the favourites.
[...]
Spirited group-stage campaign — a first-ever World Cup win is the realistic ambition, with knockout qualification a long shot.
[...]
Panama are the outsiders to qualify from Group L. Their season hinges on the opener against Ghana — a result there could keep alive hopes of a best-third-place finish in the expanded format. More likely, Panama will be competitive but fall short of the knockout rounds, with a maiden World Cup win or point representing genuine success. Projected: spirited group-stage campaign; a first-ever World Cup win is the realistic ambition, with knockout qualification a long shot.
